Attribute.value:
title: Print Spooler Named Pipe Creation (Possible Token-Impersonation Staging)
id: 3a0e534f-01ba-4ef6-bdac-99a3528c5f3b
status: experimental
description: >-
  Detects creation of a named pipe whose name contains the Print Spooler
  service pipe name (spoolss), which the lpe.exe wrapper's token-impersonation
  staging is associated with. The rule tests the pipe name only and does not
  identify the creating process, so it is not specific to lpe.exe. PipeName-only telemetry cannot correlate which process or API
  sequence created the pipe, so this is a hunting lead rather than an alert;
  pair with process-access telemetry for higher confidence.
references:
    - https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/arsenal-237-lpe-exe-detections/
author: The Hunters Ledger
date: '2026-01-25'
modified: '2026-10-10'
tags:
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.stealth
    - attack.t1134.001
    - detection.emerging-threats
logsource:
    product: windows
    category: pipe_created
detection:
    selection:
        PipeName|contains: 'spoolss'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate Print Spooler activity on hosts with print services enabled (common)
level: medium
Attribute.comment: Print Spooler Named Pipe Creation (Possible Token-Impersonation Staging) | TIER: Hunting | robustness 2 | confidence MODERATE | ATT&CK T1134.001 | rule hash 0eff31c2 | https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/arsenal-237-lpe-exe-detections/

Attribute.value:
title: Process Access to SYSTEM Processes with Token-Duplication Access Rights
id: 41794664-1101-4fbf-a117-c8c1a1f7f473
status: experimental
description: >-
  Detects a process opening a handle to winlogon.exe, lsass.exe, services.exe
  or csrss.exe with a granted access mask of 0x0440 or 0x1440, which is the
  PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION | PROCESS_DUP_HANDLE request (with and without
  PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) the Arsenal-237 lpe.exe token-theft loop
  makes before it duplicates a token. The rule does not see the later
  OpenProcessToken, DuplicateTokenEx or ImpersonateLoggedOnUser calls:
  Sysmon call traces hold module and offset frames, not function names.
references:
    - https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/arsenal-237-lpe-exe-detections/
author: The Hunters Ledger
date: '2026-01-25'
modified: '2026-10-10'
tags:
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.stealth
    - attack.t1134.001
    - detection.emerging-threats
logsource:
    product: windows
    category: process_access
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith:
            - '\winlogon.exe'
            - '\lsass.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
        GrantedAccess:
            - '0x0440'
            - '0x1440'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Security, monitoring and management software that opens these processes for token or handle duplication
level: medium
Attribute.comment: Process Access to SYSTEM Processes with Token-Duplication Access Rights | TIER: Hunting | robustness 2 | confidence LOW | ATT&CK T1134.001 | rule hash 8324f0c0 | https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/arsenal-237-lpe-exe-detections/

Attribute.value:
title: Scheduled Task Created as SYSTEM
id: 19fbc402-5876-4f9b-905b-b5452dc7d634
status: experimental
description: >-
  Detects scheduled task creation with SYSTEM privileges via direct use of
  schtasks.exe by an account whose name contains neither SYSTEM nor
  Administrator (the rule matches the account name and does not test
  membership in the Administrators group). Task names are
  likely randomized at runtime, so detection anchors on the /ru SYSTEM
  parameter rather than any specific task name.
references:
    - https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/arsenal-237-lpe-exe-detections/
author: The Hunters Ledger
date: '2026-01-25'
modified: '2026-10-10'
tags:
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.execution
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.t1053.005
    - detection.emerging-threats
logsource:
    product: windows
    category: process_creation
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
        CommandLine|contains|all:
            - '/create'
            - '/ru'
            - 'SYSTEM'
    filter_admin:
        User|contains:
            - 'SYSTEM'
            - 'Administrator'
    condition: selection and not filter_admin
falsepositives:
    - System administrators manually creating SYSTEM tasks (should be reviewed)
    - Legitimate administrative scripts using schtasks.exe
level: high
Attribute.comment: Scheduled Task Created as SYSTEM | TIER: Detection | robustness 3 | confidence HIGH | ATT&CK T1053.005 | rule hash fb3563c5 | https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/arsenal-237-lpe-exe-detections/

Attribute.value:
title: UAC Bypass via Ms-Settings Registry Hijack (lpe.exe)
id: 78ff8cac-3e71-42c5-9fdf-acdb038ce94a
status: experimental
description: >-
  Detects fodhelper.exe launched with reg.exe or lpe.exe as its parent
  process, the process-creation signature of the ms-settings registry-hijack
  UAC bypass. fodhelper.exe is a Microsoft-signed LOLBIN rarely spawned by
  reg.exe or by an unsigned executable.
references:
    - https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/arsenal-237-lpe-exe-detections/
author: The Hunters Ledger
date: '2026-01-25'
tags:
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.stealth
    - attack.t1548.002
    - detection.emerging-threats
    - stp.3
logsource:
    product: windows
    category: process_creation
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith: '\fodhelper.exe'
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\reg.exe'
            - '\lpe.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate software installation (extremely rare)
level: high
Attribute.comment: UAC Bypass via Ms-Settings Registry Hijack | TIER: Detection | robustness 2 | confidence HIGH | ATT&CK T1548.002 | rule hash f19eadae | https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/arsenal-237-lpe-exe-detections/

Attribute.value:
title: WMIC Process Call Create by a User Not Named SYSTEM or Administrator
id: 7e7d8199-93c4-4f53-ad05-84c4f3a08a96
status: experimental
description: >-
  Detects WMIC being used to create a process via the "process call create"
  syntax from a user whose name contains neither SYSTEM nor Administrator, a
  known LOLBin technique for local or remote process creation that the lpe.exe
  wrapper uses as one of its five escalation paths. The rule does not identify
  the calling process, so it is not specific to lpe.exe. WMIC process creation is also common in legitimate
  remote-administration and deployment tooling, so this is a hunting lead
  rather than an alert.
references:
    - https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/arsenal-237-lpe-exe-detections/
author: The Hunters Ledger
date: '2026-01-25'
modified: '2026-10-10'
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1047
    - detection.emerging-threats
logsource:
    product: windows
    category: process_creation
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith: '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains|all:
            - 'process'
            - 'call'
            - 'create'
    filter_admin:
        User|contains:
            - 'SYSTEM'
            - 'Administrator'
    condition: selection and not filter_admin
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts and RMM/deployment tooling using WMIC (common)
level: medium
Attribute.comment: WMIC Process Call Create by a User Not Named SYSTEM or Administrator | TIER: Hunting | robustness 2 | confidence MODERATE | ATT&CK T1047 | rule hash 86ca5224 | https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/arsenal-237-lpe-exe-detections/

rule Arsenal237_LPE_Token_Manipulation {
   meta:
      description = "Detects lpe.exe-class Arsenal-237 privilege-escalation wrappers via the full six-API token-theft sequence (process enumeration through impersonation) combined with references to at least two SYSTEM-privileged target processes."
      license = "CC BY 4.0 - https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/"
      author = "The Hunters Ledger"
      reference = "https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/arsenal-237-lpe-exe-detections/"
      date = "2026-01-25"
      hash1 = "c4dda7b5c5f6eab49efc86091377ab08275aa951d956a5485665954830d1267e"
      family = "Arsenal-237-LPE-Wrapper"
      malware_type = "Privilege-Escalation-Wrapper"
      campaign = "Arsenal-237-109.230.231.37-Malware-Repository"
      id = "b3e63cd7-eb13-5f0d-ac24-a89c0c56aa01"
   strings:
      $api1 = "CreateToolhelp32Snapshot" ascii wide
      $api2 = "OpenProcessToken" ascii wide
      $api3 = "DuplicateTokenEx" ascii wide
      $api4 = "ImpersonateLoggedOnUser" ascii wide
      $api5 = "Process32FirstW" ascii wide
      $api6 = "Process32NextW" ascii wide

      $process1 = "winlogon.exe" ascii wide nocase
      $process2 = "lsass.exe" ascii wide nocase
      $process3 = "services.exe" ascii wide nocase
      $process4 = "csrss.exe" ascii wide nocase
   condition:
      uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and
      filesize < 1MB and
      all of ($api*) and
      2 of ($process*)
}
Attribute.comment: Token Manipulation API Sequence | TIER: Detection | robustness 2 | confidence HIGH | ATT&CK T1134.001 | rule hash d5b38436 | https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/arsenal-237-lpe-exe-detections/

Broader and noisier than the native API sequence; treat as a triage lead, not an alert."

rule Arsenal237_LPE_Named_Pipe_Token_Theft {
   meta:
      description = "Detects lpe.exe-class Arsenal-237 privilege-escalation wrappers performing named-pipe token impersonation: the CreateNamedPipeW, ConnectNamedPipe, and ImpersonateNamedPipeClient API sequence together with the pipe namespace prefix and a Print Spooler (spoolss) pipe reference."
      license = "CC BY 4.0 - https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/"
      author = "The Hunters Ledger"
      reference = "https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/arsenal-237-lpe-exe-detections/"
      date = "2026-01-25"
      hash1 = "c4dda7b5c5f6eab49efc86091377ab08275aa951d956a5485665954830d1267e"
      family = "Arsenal-237-LPE-Wrapper"
      malware_type = "Privilege-Escalation-Wrapper"
      campaign = "Arsenal-237-109.230.231.37-Malware-Repository"
      id = "0f7e11be-769c-5dfe-b6f0-80c143501fcd"
   strings:
      $pipe1 = "CreateNamedPipeW" ascii wide
      $pipe2 = "ImpersonateNamedPipeClient" ascii wide
      $pipe3 = "ConnectNamedPipe" ascii wide
      $pipe4 = "\\\\.\\pipe\\" ascii wide
      $pipe5 = "spoolss" ascii wide nocase
   condition:
      uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and
      filesize < 1MB and
      all of ($pipe*)
}
